mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from its recent trough, weekday trip chains resume and retail visits rise within four weeks. The mechanism predicts RETAIL_REC will move up after a short lag because more commuting creates more incidental shopping opportunities.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -25.7 at t-1w and recovered to -8.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days after WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A jump in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent range signals intensified household errand consolidation, which spills into nearby retail and recreation trips within one week. When grocery-stop intensity is unusually high, RETAIL_REC should improve quickly as consumers combine errands.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 15 points, or retail weakens despite the threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain depressed, cross-town access to retail corridors stays constrained and retail activity falls over the next four weeks. The mechanism is strongest when both series are below their recent two-week average, indicating reduced commuting and city-center visitation.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -27.3 at t-1w and WORKPLACES was -25.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below their recent average for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL together with weaker TRANSIT indicates more time spent near home, which shifts demand away from discretionary retail and recreation within two weeks. The claim is falsified if more home-stay does not coincide with softer retail mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive while TRANSIT remained deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is above 3 points and TRANSIT remains below -15 points.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS drops sharply from a positive week to a negative week, it signals a pullback in out-of-home leisure that also weakens retail-and-recreation demand over the next two weeks. Retail should soften when discretionary outdoor activity is abruptly interrupted.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 0.4 at t-1w to -5.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decrease over the next 14 days after PARKS falls by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: During reopening, concurrent improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should translate into higher retail visits over four weeks because more commuting and downtown presence generate customer traffic. The signal fails if commuting improves without any retail pickup.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rebounded from -25.7 at t-1w to -8.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rise in PARKS combined with stable or rising GROCERY_PHARM indicates good-weather local activity that spills into shopping and dining within one week. Retail should increase quickly when outdoor activity broadens rather than concentrates at home.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive after being negative the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -8.4 at t-2w to 0.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after PARKS turns positive while GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: When mobility is simultaneously concentrated at home and away from transit hubs, retail demand is displaced for the next four weeks. The mechanism implies that a high RESIDENTIAL reading paired with persistently weak TRANSIT will precede lower RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline while TRANSIT stayed below baseline in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and TRANSIT stays below baseline throughout the period.
